name: Affordable Robotic & Automation Ltd
title: Affordable Robotic & Automation Ltd - 541402 - Conference Call With Investors And Analysts - Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to 14.45% from 8.96% on 4% lower revenue; consolidated PAT turned to ₹6.97 Cr profit from a ₹11.65 Cr loss.
summary.overview: FY26 was framed as a transformation year: management chose selective, higher-margin projects over volume, and standalone total income fell to ₹11,093 lakh from ₹16,069 lakh. Consolidated EBITDA swung to ₹1,716 lakh (14.19% margin) from a loss of ₹233 lakh, helped by about ₹151 lakh of GST provision reversal and ₹130 lakh of ODI loan interest in other income. Humro (ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary) secured a ₹48 Cr strategic investment, which will dilute ARAPL's holding below 50% once allotment completes. Management stopped giving numerical guidance, citing only a directional aim to beat FY26 "much much better".

segments.name: Automation (ARAPL, domestic)
segments.commentary: Welding lines for automotive OEMs such as Honda, Magna, Tata, Mahindra and Suzuki. Order book ₹4,496 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹2,696 lakh plus ₹1,800 lakh new bookings, per the presentation). Management said the verticals' combined book is about ₹127 Cr.

segments.name: Car parking (ARAPL)
segments.commentary: Multilevel parking, with customers including Lodha. Order book ₹820 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹580 lakh, new ₹155 lakh per the slide). Management plans to start exporting parking products in 6-9 months and to scale domestically.

segments.name: Warehouse automation (Humro / ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobile robots and WES for Fortune 50 customers; about 15 units and roughly $25,000 per month of revenue since December 2025. Order book ~$3 Mn (30-35 units, lease model, ₹36 Cr); outright-sale pipeline ~₹60 Cr. Target 225 robots in FY27, which management has not revised.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance; management said it has stopped giving number guidance and expects FY27 to be 'much much better' than FY26.
Humro FY27 target of 225 robots maintained; management said demand is 'much more' than supply.
Humro margin target of 15-18% on RaaS and outright sales, described as a moving target. Management said year-one EBITDA is not the focus; the aim is 15-20 good customers.
Next-quarter timing: Q1 is seasonally weak and profitability is expected from Q2 onward.
Humro pricing aim to cut prices by 50% over the next two years, with product-level price deflation.
ARAPL's first new product (exportable) targeted for mechanical completion in June/July 2026 and readiness by November/December 2026; radical growth expected in FY28.
capex_capacity: Five plants covering 350,000 sq ft; around 300 permanent staff and 100 contract workers (per the chairman's remarks).
Humro in-house manufacturing line: first product targeted by end-June 2026, a second model by August, and five products manufactured locally this year.
Humro inventory in the US is about 29 units, of which 5-6 are demos and 5-6 are in sales. About 20 units are to be commercially sold, with 12-15 already deployed.
FY27 deployment schedule: first 15 units ship around end-June/first week of July 2026 and a further 10 around 15 July, for deployment July-September; a further 50-60 units are being built.
Planned US strategic partner to hold local inventory, cutting delivery lead time from about 4 months to about 15 days.
demand_pricing: Humro's ₹36 Cr lease-model book equates to about $100,000 per month of lease rental; about $25,000 per month is currently billing, with $75,000 expected within one to two months.
Management said it is priced around 15-20% below Chinese competitors; named US competitors are Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav.
Management said the April-May 2026 Humro deployments were nil; 24 units were contracted and expected to deploy over the next couple of months.
Order timelines for automation work have slipped 6-8 months as customers deferred spending (per management), and some orders were rejected on profitability.

Domestic AMR opportunity: management says customers importing more than 500 AMRs from China into India are being targeted as a substitute. Management said it will not take low-margin India execution work.

qa_highlights.question: How many Humro robots were deployed in April-May against the 225-unit FY27 target, and is the target being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: No new installs in April-May; 24 units were contracted for deployment in the following months. Management said there is no revision to the 225-unit target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue fall sharply when the Q3 call indicated flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it rejected low-margin orders and added a cost-control department. Customers also deferred timelines by 6-8 months from February 2026 amid a global constraint, which delayed dispatch and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does Humro compare with competitors on quality and price in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav, saying they are about two years ahead. It claims pricing 15-20% below Chinese offers and cites technology, Indian software and easy integration as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹48 Cr investment will go to which uses, and what happens to ARAPL's holding?
qa_highlights.answer: The ARAPL holding is 83% now and will drop below 50% once allotment completes. Most funds go to operations and marketing, with some to product development; management said it does not plan local US manufacturing for now.

qa_highlights.question: Can minority shareholders still benefit after Humro is no longer a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARAPL will consolidate its share of around 43-45% of Humro profit, and that minority benefits are intact. No detailed structure was given.

risks_watch: Humro's execution: deployments have slipped, with only about $25,000 per month of revenue against a $100,000 per month lease target.
Dilution of ARAPL's stake in Humro below 50% and the consolidation impact (around 43-45% share of profit), which minority shareholders questioned.
Dependence on imported components (motors, motor controllers and radar sensors) that management said are European or Japanese brands but imported via China.
US tariff exposure, which management said has come down from 50% to 25% (and about 20-22% now), with a further policy change expected within two years.
Order-book slippage in automation: customers deferring timelines by 6-8 months.
Lack of numerical guidance for FY27 and FY28, plus Q1 seasonal losses.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the Humro pipeline, but evasive on numbers: management declined to give revenue or margin guidance and repeatedly redirected questions on FY27 revenue and Humro's quantified economics.

We are very, very competitively priced, around 15 to 20 percent lower than what the Chinese are offering.
So, number guidance or margin guidance we have stopped giving.
So, my sole target is to reduce the price by 50% in next two years.

growth.why: Management stopped numeric guidance, saying only FY27 will be 'much much better' than FY26; Humro's 225-robot FY27 target is held but billing is only ~$25k/month against it, with customer deferrals of 6-8 months and April-May Humro deployments nil, so backing is partial and the outlook is flat.
